displayedInputs.question:
An “\(n\)-pointed star” is formed as follows: the sides of a convex polygon are numbered consecutively \(1,\) \(2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(k,\) \(\ldots,\) \(n,\) \(n\geq5;\) for all \(n\) values of \(k,\) sides \(k\) and \(k+2\) are non-parallel, sides \(n+1\) and \(n+2\) being respectively identical with sides \(1\) and \(2;\) prolong the \(n\) pairs of sides numbered \(k\) and \(k+2\) until they meet. (A figure is shown for the case \(n=5.\))

[Figure 1](attached-image-1)

Let \(S\) be the degree-sum of the interior angles at the \(n\) points of the star; then \(S\) equals:

Triangle \(ABC\) is inscribed in a circle with center \(O'.\) A circle with center \(O\) is inscribed in triangle \(ABC.\) \(AO\) is drawn, and extended to intersect the larger circle in \(D.\) Then we must have:

[Figure 1](attached-image-2)

In this figure \(AB\) is a diameter of a circle, centered at \(O,\) with radius \(a.\) A chord \(AD\) is drawn and extended to meet the tangent to the circle at \(B,\) in point \(C.\) Point \(E\) is taken on \(AC\) so that \(AE=DC.\) If the coordinates of \(E\) are \((x,y),\) then:

[Figure 1](attached-image-3)

In this diagram semi-circles are constructed on diameters \(AB,\) \(AC,\) and \(CB,\) so that they are mutually tangent. If \(CD\perp AB,\) then the ratio of the shaded area to the area of a circle with \(CD\) as radius is:

[Figure 1](attached-image-4)

In this diagram, not drawn to scale, figures \(\mathrm{I}\) and \(\mathrm{III}\) are equilateral triangular regions with respective areas of \(32\sqrt3\) and \(8\sqrt3\) square inches. Figure \(\mathrm{II}\) is a square region with area \(32\) square inches. Let the length of segment \(AD\) be decreased by \(12\dfrac12\%\) of itself, while the lengths of \(AB\) and \(CD\) remain unchanged. The percent decrease in the area of the square is:

[Figure 1](attached-image-5)

In this diagram the center of the circle is \(O,\) the radius is \(a\) inches, chord \(EF\) is parallel to chord \(CD,\) \(O,\) \(G,\) \(H,\) \(J\) are collinear, and \(G\) is the midpoint of \(CD.\) Let \(K\) (square inches) represent the area of trapezoid \(CDFE\) and let \(R\) (square inches) represent the area of rectangle \(ELMF.\) Then, as \(CD\) and \(EF\) are translated upward so that \(OG\) increases toward the value \(a,\) while \(JH\) always equals \(HG,\) the ratio \(K:R\) becomes arbitrarily close to:

[Figure 1](attached-image-6)

A parabolic arch has a height of \(16\) inches and a span of \(40\) inches. The height, in inches, of the arch at a point \(5\) inches from the center \(M,\) is:

[Figure 1](attached-image-7)

Let \(OABC\) be a unit square in the \(xy\)-plane with \(O(0,0),\) \(A(1,0),\) \(B(1,1),\) and \(C(0,1).\) Let \(u=x^2-y^2\) and \(v=2xy\) define a transformation of the \(xy\)-plane into the \(uv\)-plane. The transform (or image) of the square is:
